note: Re-judged 2026-10-26 by an independent auditor who authored none of the change, after 394bd1e802 and 180b306ffa (spec-bgp-rs-replacement-on-withdrawal). RFC 7911 Section 2: "However, the Path Identifier MUST be assigned in such a way that the BGP speaker is able to use the (Prefix, Path Identifier) to uniquely identify a path advertised to a neighbor." The only change to a cited producer is session_ownership.go adjOutWrite.allow, which in the adjOutRecovery case now also refuses a departure withdrawal of an ADD-PATH key when the owed record spares the entry owner (recoverySpares -> adjOutOwed.spares: owner.generation > the exclusion's departed generation, i.e. a newer session's path). That branch only returns false before any owner, withdrawn or identifier bookkeeping: it mints, rebinds, releases and reuses no Path Identifier, so the recipient keeps the one (Prefix, Path Identifier) entry it already had. The identifier producers (forward_path_id.go generate/generatePath/mintLocked/release*, allow's bindSourcePath branch) and both tagged units are byte-identical; TestForwardPathIDStableAcrossUpdates (positive) still pins one stable identifier per (source, prefix, received id) and TestForwardPathIDsDifferForCollidingSources (negative) still requires distinct identifiers for colliding sources, each with a verified revert record on generatePath; both green at HEAD in a git archive export. Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgements are in this file's git history.
